messages:
maya: noticing a spike in gRPC stalls for model-serving pods across nodepair-usw-2 yesterday evening. streaming RPCs drop mid-stream, jobs retry, GPUs go idle :eyes:

alex: saw that too. kubectl logs from the sidecar show repeated `io timeout` and then `stream reset` from client. started around 18:13 PDT.

jordan: any pattern on which nodes? east-west only?

maya: yes, largely east-west between compute nodes in the same AZ (nodepool-g4-*) when flows cross a bonded uplink -> then retransmit storms. intra-node is fine.

sasha: @net-eng any recent fabric or encap changes rolled out?

net-eng: pushed a config last week to enable new geneve/encap sizing to handle extra metadata for telemetry. should be transparent but i'll double-check MTU clamping.

alex: dumped a few pcaps. seeing a lot of fragmented IP packets and `DF` set cleared on sender. Wireshark shows fragments not reassembling at destination; gRPC stream waits and then stalls. snippet:
```
17:23:41.123 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 63, id 54321, offset 0, flags [none]) 10.10.4.12 > 10.10.5.33: Flags [DF], proto TCP, length 1500
17:23:41.124 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 63, id 54321, offset 1480, flags [none]) 10.10.4.12 > 10.10.5.33: proto TCP, length 40
```

alex: sender thinks path supports 1500 but due to geneve overhead packets are being split in-flight. some switches drop the tail fragment when SR-IOV VF+encap interacts with host egress clamp.

jordan: can you share `ip link` + `ip route get` on both endpoints? also need `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc` and any iptables mss clamp rules.

maya: pasted outputs:
```
# on pod host A
ip link show eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
# on pod host B
ip link show eth0: mtu 1450 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```

maya: ah — one host had mtu clamped to 1450 by a recent kube-proxy post-renderer script for encap. mismatch explains fragmentation.

sasha: nice catch. that would create per-path fragmentation when some switches do not reassemble. gRPC streaming uses larger segments for throughput; fragment loss = stream stall.

net-eng: rolling back the geneve encaps sizing change to restore consistent MTU across nodepair-usw-2. will patch the post-renderer to set consistent MTU and add a CI check.

alex: mitigation steps: 1) enable PMTU discovery (clear ip_no_pmtu_disc), 2) add transient MSS clamp at host egress to 1400 until configs stable, 3) rollout patch to make encap overhead explicit in kube manifests.

maya: applying MSS clamp now on affected nodes, will monitor. posting a quick command for MSS clamp: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1400`

infra-bot: alert resolved? marked incident P1 -> P2 pending verification. docs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/networking/mtu-fragmentation

jordan: after MSS clamp, streaming errors dropped dramatically. keep an eye on GPU scheduling — reclaiming jobs. great work team :thumbsup:

sasha: follow-ups: add automated MTU parity checks in nodepool bootstrap, add e2e test that triggers large streaming RPCs across AZ. i'll file a ticket.

maya: thanks all — will close thread once metrics look healthy for 2h.
